title: Enterprise Onboarding — Integration, Escalation, Known Issues, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, and the recurring health check / QBR template used by Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and SRE. It is intended as the single source of truth for initial onboarding through ongoing operations for enterprise customers.

Use cases: new enterprise onboarding, annual health checks, pre-QBR readiness, cross-team escalations, and postmortem follow-ups.

Owner & Contacts

- Document owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel)
- Primary on-call contact: eng-sre oncall (pagerduty: Redwood-SRE)
- CS escalation Slack channel: #cs-esc
- Engineering escalation Slack channel: #sre-oncall
- Support email: support@redwood.ai (triage)
- Enterprise CS distribution: enterprise-cs@redwood.ai

1) Enterprise Onboarding — Phased Checklist

Phase 1 — Kickoff (Week 0–1)
- Schedule kickoff: invite CS, SE, Customer engineering, Security, and SRE.
- Deliverables: project charter, success criteria, contacts, access list.
- Action items:
  1. Confirm primary technical contact and legal/compliance approvers.
  2. Share Redwood Quickstart guide and API key provisioning steps.
  3. Create customer workspace in Console and enable role-based access.

Phase 2 — Integration (Week 1–3)
- Goals: establish API connectivity, telemetry, and baseline performance.
- Integration checklist (table):

| Item | Owner | Required before pilot? | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| API key created & scoped | CS/SE | Yes | Prefer scoped keys for prod traffic |
| VPC peering / Private link configured | Customer/Infra | If private deployment | Follow eng-private-deployments reference-arch |
| Ingesting telemetry to Customer S3/Datadog | SE | Yes | Provide example log format |
| Test prompts and eval set uploaded | Customer/CS | Yes | Baseline for quality regressions |
| Rate limit and quotas configured | CS | Yes | Set soft limits for first 30 days |

Phase 3 — Pilot & Validation (Week 3–6)
- Run 2–4 week pilot, collect metrics: latency (p50/p95), error rate, token consumption, cache hit rate.
- Validation checklist:
  - Confirm SLA alignment and failover policy.
  - Validate integration retry logic and idempotency keys.
  - Execute canary traffic (10–20%) and monitor model quality.

Phase 4 — Production Rollout
- Execute cutover plan with rollback steps.
- Hand off operational runbook to customer and CS.
- Schedule QBR cadence and access review.

2) Integration Guides — Key Recommendations

API access & best practices
- Use short-lived scoped API keys for service-to-service calls. Rotate keys every 90 days.
- Recommended retry policy:
  - Exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries for 5xx.
  - Avoid retrying 4xx except 429 (rate-limit).
- Request example (cURL):

  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-13b","input":"Summarize our onboarding plan","max_tokens":256}'

Streaming and function calls
- Prefer streaming for interactive experiences to reduce perceived latency. Implement client-side timeouts of 60s by default.
- Use function/tool calling for structured outputs and predictable schemas. Validate responses against a JSON schema on ingest.

Telemetry & observability
- Export request/response metrics (request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, status) to the customer telemetry endpoint or shared S3.
- Sample telemetry JSON: 
  {"request_id":"<uuid>","model":"redwood/gpt-13b","latency_ms":210,"status":"200"}

Security & private deployment notes
- For Private deployments: verify KMS/HSM integration and key rotation with customer security team.
- For VPC Peering: exchange subnets and ensure Security Group rules allow TCP 443 from customer egress IPs.

3) Escalation Playbook

Severity definitions and response targets
- Sev 1 (P0) — Production outage affecting >50% of requests or system-wide failover: Response target 15 minutes, mitigation checkpoint 1 hour.
- Sev 2 (P1) — Significant degradation (p95 latency > 2x SLO or errors > 5%): Response target 1 hour, mitigation checkpoint 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (P2) — Partial degradation or single-customer issues (errors > 1% for that customer): Response target 4 hours, checkpoint 24 hours.
- Sev 4 (P3) — Informational / general questions: Response target 2 business days.

Escalation matrix
- Triage (CS Support): support@redwood.ai — initial ticket creation, customer communication within response SLA.
- Engineering triage: @eng-sre (Slack) and PagerDuty (Redwood-SRE) — escalate if no mitigation within checkpoint.
- Product/Model team: loop in model-owner alias (model-owner@redwood.ai) for quality regressions.
- Executive escalation: customer success director and account executive for enterprise C-level notifications.

Steps for Sev1
1. CS opens ticket, notifies #cs-esc and oncall via PagerDuty.
2. SRE acknowledges and posts initial bridge URL.
3. Triage: collect request_id, model, timestamps, customer region, API key ID, and recent config changes.
4. Apply immediate mitigations: rollback model, switch routing to fallback region/model, throttle traffic, or enable circuit breaker.
5. Communicate cadence to customer every 30 minutes until resolved.
6. Post-incident: run a postmortem (1 week) and map action items to owners and deadlines.

Contact list (primary)
- CS triage: support@redwood.ai
- SRE oncall (PagerDuty): Redwood-SRE oncall
- SE escalation: se-team@redwood.ai
- Model quality: model-owner@redwood.ai

4) Known Issues & Workarounds (living log)

KI-2026-014 — High p95 latency after extended KV-cache growth
- Symptom: Customers with long-lived sessions see p95 latency spikes after sustained traffic (>72h) due to KV cache fragmentation.
- Impact: Increased token latency and occasional 504s for multi-turn conversations.
- Workaround: Rotate the model instance (restart), flush KV prefix cache for the customer, reduce per-connection max_seq_length to 2048 temporarily.
- Permanent fix: Runtime patch 2026.11.2 (deployed), monitor for recurrence.

KI-2027-001 — Quantized model mismatch causing hallucinations on gpt-13b-q4f
- Symptom: Generated outputs contain repeated factual inconsistencies after model upgrade.
- Impact: Quality regression for LLM-assisted search and summarization flows.
- Workaround: Pin customer to previous variant (gpt-13b-v2) and disable quantization for the route. Re-run eval set against new quantized variant in staging.
- Owner: Applied ML / Model Onboarding team.

KI-2026-022 — Rate-limit spike when batcher fallback triggers
- Symptom: Sudden 429 bursts when our batcher switches to conservative batching under GPU pressure.
- Workaround: Configure client to implement backoff, temporarily raise soft quota for pilot customers, or route to dedicated capacity.

Reporting new issues
- Submit a Jira ticket with label cs-known-issue and include: reproduction steps, request_ids, sample prompts, and affected customer IDs. Notify model-owner and eng-sre.

5) Support Process & SLAs

Ticket lifecycle
1. Ticket created in Zendesk/Support system by CS or automated ingestion.
2. Triage within SLA by CS (see severity targets above).
3. Assign to SE/SRE/Product as appropriate.
4. Provide customer-facing updates at least once per checkpoint interval until resolved.
5. Close with resolution notes, remediation steps, and link to postmortem if applicable.

Escalation triggers (auto/escalate)
- No mitigation within checkpoint window.
- Regressions repeated >3 times in 30 days for same customer.
- SLA breach potential for enterprise contract.

Operational SLAs (internal targets)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): Sev1 < 15m, Sev2 < 60m, Sev3 < 4h.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM): Sev1 < 1h, Sev2 < 4h, Sev3 < 24h.
- Customer update cadence: At least every 30m for Sev1, every 4h for Sev2, daily for Sev3 until resolved.

6) Health Checks & Quarterly Business Review (QBR) Materials

Key metrics to collect (30/90/365 day windows)
- p50/p95 latency (ms) by route and model
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and successful response rate
- Tokens consumed per hour, cost per 1k tokens (estimated)
- Cache hit rate and effective token savings
- Throughput (requests/sec) and concurrency levels
- Model regression tests pass rate (prompt-based eval suite)
- Availability / uptime (SLA compliance)

Monthly Health Check template (CS → Customer)
- Summary: One-paragraph status (Green/Yellow/Red)
- Metrics snapshot: list p95, error rate, tokens, cost delta 
- Recent changes: model upgrades, config changes, traffic spikes 
- Action items: open tickets, planned optimizations, security items

QBR Template (45–60 minutes)
- Attendees: Customer executive sponsor, technical leads, CS, SE, SRE representative
- Agenda:
  1. Executive summary & adoption highlights (5–10m)
  2. Usage & performance review (10–15m) — tokens, p95, cost trends
  3. Quality & model evaluation (10–15m) — eval pass rate, regressions
  4. Roadmap & upcoming changes (5–10m) — model variants, infra changes
  5. Action items / next steps (5–10m)
- Pre-QBR deliverables: run the eval harness against the customer prompt set, produce a one-page scorecard, and circulate 48 hours before the meeting.

QBR Scorecard (one-pager items)
- Top 3 successes (adoption features, latency improvements, cost savings)
- Top 3 risks (model regressions, security items, capacity constraints)
- Agreed actions and owners with due dates

7) Post-incident & Continuous Improvement

- Postmortem requirement: All Sev1 incidents must have a blameless postmortem published within 7 calendar days with root cause, timeline, and action owners.
- Action item tracking: Convert postmortem actions to Jira with owners and SLAs.
- Quarterly review: CS + Eng + Product review of recurring customer issues and prioritization for runtime/model fixes.

Appendices

A. Useful links

B. Example support update (email / ticket body)

Subject: [Redwood] Incident update (Ticket #12345) — current status: Mitigated

Hi <CustomerName>,

We wanted to provide an update: our oncall team identified a model routing regression related to GPU kernel selection and rolled back the model variant at 14:32 UTC. Error rates have returned to normal and we continue to monitor. Next update in 30 minutes.

Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler selected incompatible quantized kernels during peak load.
Mitigation: model rollback and temporary throttling.

Best,
Customer Success Team

C. How to report a new known issue (summary)
- Create Jira with cs-known-issue label, include: request_ids, reproduction steps, sample prompts, affected customers.
- Notify reviewers list and eng-sre channel.
